nodes.notes: Serves an n8n-hosted form (Email, Company, Score). Each submission becomes one execution.

nodes.name: Keep Valid Leads
nodes.notes: Drops items that fail the condition; only qualifying items continue (no false branch).

nodes.name: Route by Work Type
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: sales, support + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Process 'sales' → Airtable
nodes.notes: Upserts into Airtable's 'Leads' table, matched on leadId — safe to re-run without creating duplicates. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#sales) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Leads' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Merge Routed Work
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Tag Pipeline Metadata
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes pipeline, version. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Stamp Processing Time
nodes.notes: Stamps processedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 100 items to protect downstream quotas.

# Log applications: Airtable & Outlook

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers outreach work end to end across Airtable, Outlook and Slack.

It moves through 11 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Lead Form Submission
2. Keep Valid Leads
3. Route by Work Type
4. Process 'sales' → Airtable
5. Fast-Track 'support' + Alert
6. Hold Unknown Types (DLQ)
7. Merge Routed Work
8. Tag Pipeline Metadata
9. Stamp Processing Time
10. Cap Batch Volume
11. Send Summary to Outlook

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing outreach work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Lead Form Submission → Keep Valid Leads → Route by Work Type → Process 'sales' → Airtable → Fast-Track 'support' + Alert → Hold Unknown Types (DLQ) → Merge Routed Work → Tag Pipeline Metadata → Stamp Processing Time → Cap Batch Volume → Send Summary to Outlook → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Outlook

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Airtable and Outlook aligned by hand for outreach
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Airtable, for outreach
- Outreach work where "Keep Valid Leads" is still a manual step before Airtable
- Outreach work that only reaches Airtable when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Airtable and Outlook in step for outreach, without anyone re-typing a row
- A failed Airtable or Outlook call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 13 nodes in this outreach build
- Branches rejoin before Airtable, so a outreach run reports once rather than 13 times
- Fans the same result out to Slack in the same run, for outreach
- Pinned sample data ships with it — run all 13 nodes for outreach before wiring Airtable

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Microsoft OAuth2; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Unrecognized work types are parked in a dead-letter lane instead of erroring the whole run or silently dropping the item — new event kinds will show up eventually, and this is where you'd notice one without losing it. One kind is deliberately routed through a sub-workflow to show how heavier per-type logic can be extracted without touching this router at all.

## Practice exercises

Once it's wired up with real credentials, try:

1. Send a work-type value that matches no switch rule and confirm it lands in the dead-letter branch.
2. Add a new work type and its own handling branch.
3. Replace the direct-write branch with a sub-workflow call, matching the pattern already used for the first kind.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → Microsoft Graph → Mail.Send / Mail.Read.
_Gotcha:_ Choose delegated vs application permissions deliberately; they behave differently.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your outreach process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Outlook: use `Mail.Send` alone if nothing here reads the mailbox.
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.

**Do not log**
outreach payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
